description: The pie chart presents the distribution of sources/outlets referenced in the context of “Narrative Media Framing in Political Discourse,” showing 17 slices in total. The largest slice is labeled “Breitbart” in blue at approximately 14%, followed by “Other” in gray at about 13%. Two similarly sized slices, “Drudge Report” (orange) and “The Daily Caller” (green), are each about 8%, and “The Huffington Post” (red) is about 7%. Two slices labeled “NPR” (purple) and “Vox” (brown) are each about 6%, while “The Guardian” (pink) and “BBC” (light gray) are each about 5%. “RT” (yellow-green) is about 4%. The remaining seven slices are each about 3% and include “Daily Kos” (teal), “National Review” (light blue), “Daily Mail” (orange), “Redstate” (green), “Fox News” (red), “CNN” (purple), and “Shareblue PoliticusUSA” (brown/pink). Numeric percentage labels appear inside the slices, labels are placed around the pie without a separate legend, no slices appear exploded or otherwise emphasized, and the segments appear arranged roughly from larger to smaller values around the chart.
